articles.title: Tamil Nadu's Thiruparankundram Deepam Row: 100 Years of Dispute & 5 Key Courtroom Milestones
articles.description: The Thiruparankundram Deepam controversy has a legal history spanning more than a century. From the 1920 ownership dispute between the Subramaniaswamy temple and the dargah to successive Madras High Court rulings in 1996, 2014 and 2017, the question of where the sacred Deepam should be lit has remained contentious. While earlier court orders addressed the traditional location of the ritual and the limits of judicial intervention in religious practices, a December 2025 Madras High Court order allowing devotees to light the Deepam at the Deepathoon reignited the controversy. How did a dispute over ownership evolve into a battle over religious traditions, temple administration and judicial authority? Here's the legal timeline behind the Thiruparankundram Deepam row.

articles.title: Akhilesh’s 26-Seat Offer, Congress’s 100-Plus Demand: Alliance Talks Hit Roadblock | News18
articles.description: The political contest for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections is gathering momentum, but the proposed Samajwadi Party-Congress alliance is facing a serious test over seat-sharing. The tensions come as SP chief Akhilesh Yadav prepares to unveil the party’s ‘Jan-Man Ka Manifesto’ on Constitution Day, outlining its political and policy priorities for the state. At the centre of the dispute is a widening gap between the two parties’ expectations. The Samajwadi Party has reportedly offered Congress 26 seats, while Congress has sought more than 100 constituencies. The disagreement has intensified after the SP announced five candidates even as negotiations remained underway. articles.title: Bhagwat praises India’s youth as ‘authentic’, urges them to follow unsung heroes at Padma festival
articles.description: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat praised India's younger generation as authentic and said today's youth value honesty, reject falsehood and have the enthusiasm to dedicate themselves to causes they believe in. Addressing the 5th edition of the Padmaa Festival in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Bhagwat said young Indians want to make the country great. He urged them to draw inspiration from Padma awardees and unsung heroes who have dedicated their lives to serving society. Bhagwat also emphasised that appreciating such individuals is not enough; their work must be carried forward by the next generation.
